extracted.intended_audience: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship researchers and their host institutions (beneficiaries)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on implementing and complying with the legal, administrative, reporting, mobility, open science and financial requirements of a Marie Skłodowska‑Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship under Horizon Europe. Intended to be used by the researcher and the host institution to manage the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher Mobility Declaration (MD) submission and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mobility Declaration must be submitted via the Portal within 20 days of the project start date, be kept up-to-date throughout the project lifetime and represent an accurate reflection of how the project is being implemented at any point in time. The MD must be submitted by a representative of the beneficiary (host institution), not by the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MD can be reopened by the Project Officer for changes; updates should reflect periods of activity, suspensions, part-time work, secondments, etc. After each change the MD should be submitted to the PO. Guidance on how to use the MD is provided in this document and on the Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project start date options and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Two start date options: (1) fixed start date as specified in the grant agreement, or (2) first day of the month after entry into force of the grant agreement. The actual start date must not be later than 1 September of the year following signature of the grant agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If problems are anticipated, notify the PO as soon as possible. Start dates cannot be changed retroactively. Starting earlier or later may require an amendment; short delays can be encoded as a 'generic suspension' in the MD but amendments to extend end date must be requested ~2 months before original end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary (host institution) employment and supervision obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution (Beneficiary) is the researcher’s employer for the project duration and must provide an employment contract (or equivalent) with full social security coverage, host the researcher at its premises, and provide adequate supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The researcher should inform the host institution of any events likely to affect employment or project implementation; the beneficiary must inform REA of events likely to affect or delay project implementation (Article 19). See Annex 5 of the grant agreement for obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time and exclusivity requirement (with part-time exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers are required to work full-time and exclusively on the MSCA‑PF project for its duration, unless part-time work is agreed and authorised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-time is possible if (a) the PO has been consulted, (b) agreed between researcher and host, (c) researcher remains at host premises for time charged to project, (d) researcher works minimum 50% FTE on the project, and (e) encoded correctly in the MD with new recruitment periods for each part-time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for professional part-time work
rubrics_metrics.description: Where part-time work is to combine MSCA‑PF with another professional activity, additional conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable time records must be kept; researcher must not undertake the same research in more than one project; no double-charging of costs; researcher must not benefit from two MSCA grants simultaneously; total professional time commitment must not exceed 100% FTE; part-time must not jeopardise research and training activities. For Global Fellowships, professional part-time cannot take place during the outgoing phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspensions and encoding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any period of absence of more than 30 consecutive days must be encoded as a suspension (0% work) in the MD. During generic suspensions no unit contribution can be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspensions (other than long-term leave) should not exceed 30% of project duration. Each suspension period must be encoded in the MD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term leave allowance and encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: If absence >30 consecutive days results in costs to the host not covered by social security (maternity, paternity, parental, sick, special leave), additional costs can be charged to the project as a long-term leave allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss with PO; beneficiary must encode these as long-term leave selecting specific reason in MD and indicate the percentage reflecting the amount the beneficiary is required to cover under national legislation (may change over time; encode changes as separate periods). If full costs are covered by national social security, encode long-term leave with contribution percentage 0%. During such periods no unit contribution can be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleworking restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Teleworking from abroad is not permitted because MSCA is a researcher mobility programme; limited teleworking from the same country as the host can be accepted under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telework from same country must be agreed with host institution, be for limited period (e.g., one day a week), must not interfere with correct implementation of the project, and PO should be consulted beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income restrictions and top-up rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must not receive additional income for research and training activities conducted in the context of the project, except for 'top-up' amounts paid by or via the host institution or an institution listed in Annex 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any additional income complies with grant rules; update MD if family status changes affecting allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments requirement and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive changes to the proposed work or its implementation must be agreed with REA beforehand and, in some cases, via an amendment. Events requiring an amendment include transfer of grant to new beneficiary, change of secondment host, increase in maximum grant amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments should be discussed with host institution and PO and requested before the actual change occurs. Amendments cannot be submitted in IT system after project end date. Some changes encoded in MD that impact end date require an amendment ~2 months before original end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Notifications (changes requiring notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain changes require a Formal Notification rather than an amendment. These include changes to the scientific supervisor (with justification and CV), important changes in scientific direction, and changes affecting ability to implement the project as planned (e.g., travel difficulty, unavailable infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult PO beforehand and submit Formal Notification well before the scheduled change. Approved supervisor changes should also be encoded in the MD.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request amendments or Formal Notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and Formal Notifications must be launched through the Portal under 'Manage Project' > 'Launch a new interaction with the EU', completing the 'AMD Justification' description box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once prepared, send for review by clicking 'Lock for review' and 'EU review'. The amendment is the formal responsibility of the host institution (not the researcher). The system may auto-select relevant amendment clauses; some must be selected by the PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated partners encoding and secondments
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions contributing to project implementation (hosting periods of research) must be encoded as associated partners in the grant agreement and in the MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondments may be to institutions worldwide. For European Fellowships secondments max 1/3 of project normal duration (e.g., max 8 months for 24-month project); for Global Fellowships secondments up to 1/3 of outgoing phase; maximum 3 months of secondments can be at beneficiary at project start. Secondments are contractual if indicated in Annex 1 and changes require an amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short visits vs secondments
rubrics_metrics.description: Short visits are mobility outside host premises for limited periods (e.g., fieldwork), supervised directly by the institution, represent only a small part of the project and should not be encoded in the MD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt whether an activity qualifies as a short visit, consult the PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Academic Placements (NAPs) eligibility and encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: NAPs must be requested at proposal submission, take place after normal project duration, be at premises of a non-academic institution in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, and must appear in the core grant agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAPs are encoded in MD under 'Secondment Information' by ticking 'Inter-Sectoral Research Placement' and specifying dates. Salary continues to be paid by host institution during NAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated partners during Global Fellowship outgoing phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The third-country hosting institution during the outgoing phase is an associated partner and must be encoded in the grant agreement and the MD, including duration and suspensions. Time at the beneficiary during the outgoing phase (up to 3 months) need not be encoded separately but must be agreed with PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encode secondments for outgoing phase in MD; consult PO for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access obligation for scientific publications
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer-reviewed scientific publications (including long-text formats) arising from the project must be made available open access immediately upon publication with no restrictions, by depositing either the final peer-reviewed manuscript or final published version in a trusted repository under CC BY or a licence with equivalent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No embargo periods permitted. Researchers must retain sufficient IP rights to comply. Repository entries must include information needed to validate conclusions; links to publisher and repository must be provided in the Continuous Reporting section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata requirements for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata of deposited publications must be open under CC0 or equivalent and provide at least: publication author(s), title, date, venue; acknowledgement of Horizon Europe funding; grant project name, acronym, number; licensing terms; persistent identifiers for publication, authors and, if possible, organisations and grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include persistent identifiers for any research outputs/tools needed to validate conclusions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Data Management (RDM) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must manage digital research data responsibly, in line with FAIR principles, by submitting and regularly updating a Data Management Plan (DMP), depositing data in a trusted repository as soon as possible within DMP deadlines, and ensuring open access under CC BY or CC0 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access restrictions must be justified in the DMP. Metadata for data must be open under CC0 and include dataset description, deposit date, authors, venue, embargo info, Horizon Europe funding and persistent identifiers for datasets, authors and related outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP) submission deadline and template
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMP is compulsory and must be submitted as a Deliverable within the first 6 months of the project. A voluntary EC DMP template is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DMP should outline what data will be collected/generated, methodology, standards, sharing arrangements, curation and preservation. Deposit data in trusted repository (e.g., Zenodo) and enable third-party access, mining, exploitation, reproduction and dissemination free of charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of EU funding and visual identity
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications and dissemination (publications, posters, conference papers, etc.) must ensure visibility of the EU flag and acknowledge EU funding in the prescribed manner (Article 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EU image can be downloaded from provided link; further communications guidance available on REA website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Reporting module and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous Reporting must be kept updated via the Portal throughout project implementation. Compulsory deliverables for MSCA‑PF: Data Management Plan (by month 6), Career Development Plan (by month 6), Dissemination/Communication/Outreach Plan (by penultimate month), and Ethics Deliverables where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverables uploaded under 'Continuous Reporting data' > 'Deliverables' tab. Only one document per deliverable may be uploaded (merge or zip files). Avoid including personal data except researcher name and project acronym/number because public deliverables will be published via CORDIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan (CDP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must ensure the researcher establishes a Career Development Plan with their supervisor outlining training requirements, research objectives and career goals. The CDP must be submitted as a Deliverable by month 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal template required; CDP can include transferable skills training, teaching, planning publications, conference participation and citizen engagement. Host must support implementation; CDP can be updated as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication, dissemination and exploitation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are required to engage in communication (targeted info to multiple audiences), dissemination (share results with potential users, peers, policymakers via publications), and exploitation (pursue use of results via further research, products, services) of project results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start planning early; exploitation activities should be pursued up to four years after project end. Keep PO informed of media activities so REA can help ensure coverage. Further guidance available in Programme Guide and REA website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher unit contributions (allowances) definitions and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher unit contributions are fixed amounts paid to the researcher: Living Allowance (gross, adjusted by country correction coefficient), Mobility Allowance (to cover moving costs), and Family Allowance (if entitled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must provide clear overview of gross and net monthly allowance. Country correction coefficients apply to whole country. For Global Fellowships different coefficients apply for outgoing and return phases. Family status changes must be updated in MD; an amendment to increase max grant amount is normally required before project end to reflect family allowance addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family allowance definition and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Family is defined as persons linked by marriage (or equivalent recognised relationship) or dependent children actually maintained by the researcher. Family Allowance entitles the researcher to an additional monthly allowance as of the date eligibility begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change of family status requires new recruitment line in MD; host may need amendment to increase max EU contribution; in the meantime host meets additional cost and is reimbursed by REA at next reporting period end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eurozone currency reporting and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project budget is calculated and paid in EURO; hosts must report costs in EURO. Where allowances are not paid in EURO, payments may fluctuate due to exchange rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host may underpay monthly to hedge exchange fluctuations as long as researcher receives correct amount by latest project end. Hosts normally report costs using average official daily exchange rates over reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional unit contributions categories and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional unit contributions are fixed monthly amounts managed by the host to cover professional costs and are divided into Research, Training and Network Contribution (to cover training, conferences, consumables, visas, secondments) and Management and Indirect Contribution (to cover host institution’s involvement costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional unit costs can be shared with associated partners (e.g., to cover secondments or NAPs). These amounts are normally administered by the host, not the researcher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special needs allowance eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: If the researcher has a disability that would prevent participation without additional financial support, host can request a 'special needs' allowance to cover items/services not funded from other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss request with PO; if accepted, update MD and an amendment to increase max grant amount may be required before project end.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSCA Green Charter and sustainability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers and beneficiaries should make best-effort to minimise environmental impact of research (minimise waste/emissions, prioritise low-carbon mobility, use renewable energy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Report will ask how Green Charter principles were integrated. Guidance and inspiration available on MSCA webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Report submission deadline and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Report must be submitted within 60 days following the project end date; submission is a precondition for payment of remaining amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must cover scientific progress and deviations, training and knowledge transfer activities, secondments, career development, project management, dissemination and communication activities, and overall impact. Submission is the formal responsibility of the institution; a separate financial report must be submitted by the legal representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Evaluation and Follow-up Questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded MSCA researchers are required to submit two questionnaires about their experience: an Evaluation Questionnaire immediately after project completion and a Follow-up Questionnaire two years later (Article 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questionnaires accessed via provided links; project-related information (project number, acronym) will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication with Project Officer (PO) via Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact with the Project Officer should take place exclusively through the Communication Centre interface in the Funding & Tenders Opportunities Portal under 'Manage Project', unless discussing sensitive/private issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications in the Communication Centre are visible to all appointed representatives for the project. PO name is indicated in the Portal; phone and email available via EU Whoiswho.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverable upload constraints and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one document can be uploaded per deliverable; avoid including personal data beyond researcher name and project acronym/number because deliverables marked 'PUB' will be made publicly available via CORDIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable merge documents before uploading or zip them. Consult Portal guidance for deliverables encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics deliverables and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project is subject to ethics review, all ethics requirements due post-start are included as Deliverables and placed in an automatically generated 'Ethics requirements' work package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulfil ethics-related deliverables as automatically scheduled; follow ethics review instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support structures and contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: First point of contact for issues should be supervisor and host administration; if unresolved, contact designated PO. National Contact Points (NCPs) and MSCA-NET provide additional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution is the employer and employment laws of the country of recruitment apply. For IT Portal issues, contact the IT Helpdesk directly. Further guidance available on Portal and REA websites.
